title_py: Jǐ gè rén? Yī dào wǔ
auditory_note: Tap ▶ Listen to play each clip.

banner.body_en: No rush on yesterday's grandpa and grandma practice. Reply to that email (or answer in chat) whenever you're ready, and I'll grade both lessons.
banner.body_py: Bú yòng zháojí. Dì-qī kè de liànxí, nǐ zhǔnbèi hǎo le jiù huífù, wǒ huì yìqǐ píngfēn.

intro.en: Hi Evan! You can already say who is in your family: dad, mom, kids, brothers, sisters, and now grandpa and grandma. Today you'll learn to count them. We'll learn the numbers one to five, the question word jǐ (how many), and a classic first question people ask in China: "How many people are in your family?" We'll also review rén (person), plus yéye, nǎinai, and Wǒ ài nǐ from yesterday.
intro.py: Nǐ hǎo, Evan! Nǐ yǐjīng huì shuō nǐ jiā yǒu shéi: bàba, māma, háizi, xiōngdì jiěmèi, hái yǒu yéye hé nǎinai. Jīntiān nǐ yào xué zěnme shǔ tāmen. Wǒmen xué yī dào wǔ, wèncí jǐ, hái yǒu yí gè hěn chángjiàn de wèntí: “Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ gè rén?” Wǒmen yě fùxí rén, hái yǒu zuótiān de yéye, nǎinai hé Wǒ ài nǐ.

blocks.note_en: High, flat 1st tone. Heads up: right before a 4th tone it rises to yí, so "one person" is yí gè rén.
blocks.note_py: Dì-yī shēng, gāo ér píng. Zài dì-sì shēng qiánmiàn biànchéng yí: yí gè rén.

blocks.note_en: 3rd-tone dip. When you count people or things, use liǎng, not èr: liǎng gè háizi means two kids. You already used this in Lesson 4!
blocks.note_py: Dì-sān shēng. Shǔ rén huò dōngxi de shíhou, yòng liǎng, bú yòng èr: liǎng gè háizi.

blocks.note_en: High, flat 1st tone, like singing one long note.
blocks.note_py: Dì-yī shēng, xiàng chàng yí gè cháng yīn.

blocks.note_en: Sharp 4th-tone drop. Say "sih" with a short, firm push.

blocks.note_py: Dì-sān shēng, xiān xià zài shàng.

blocks.note_en: A question word for small amounts, usually under ten. Like shéi, it sits right where the number would go.
blocks.note_py: Wèn xiǎo shùliàng de wèncí. Gēn shéi yíyàng, tā fàng zài shùzì de wèizhi.

blocks.en: How many people are in your family?
blocks.py: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ gè rén?
blocks.note_en: Word by word: you family have how-many (counter) person? Watch the tones: yǒu jǐ is two 3rd tones in a row, so say yóu jǐ.
blocks.note_py: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ gè rén? Yǒu jǐ shì liǎng gè dì-sān shēng, suǒyǐ shuō yóu jǐ.

blocks.title: 🔑 Pattern: number + gè + noun
blocks.body_en: In Chinese you can't put a number right next to a noun. You need a little counter word in between, and gè is the all-purpose one. To ask, just swap the number for jǐ. No ma needed, since jǐ already makes it a question.
blocks.body_py: Zài Zhōngwén lǐ, shùzì hé míngcí zhōngjiān yào yǒu liàngcí. Gè shì zuì chángyòng de. Wèn de shíhou, bǎ shùzì huànchéng jǐ. Bú yòng jiā ma.

blocks.title: 🎵 Tone tip: yī changes, liǎng doesn't
blocks.body_en: Because gè is 4th tone, yī becomes yí in yí gè. Write it as you say it: yí gè rén. The other numbers keep their tones: liǎng gè, sān gè, sì gè, wǔ gè.
blocks.body_py: Yīnwèi gè shì dì-sì shēng, yī biànchéng yí: yí gè rén. Qítā shùzì bú biàn: liǎng gè, sān gè, sì gè, wǔ gè.

blocks.en: These four are due for review. Listen to each one and say it out loud before Practice.
blocks.py: Zhè sì gè cí yào fùxí le. Liànxí yǐqián, qǐng tīng yíxià, ránhòu dàshēng shuō.

rows.tip: rise on YÉ, then a soft ye
dip on NǍI, then a soft nai
